title: EFG Lease Classifier — UCC §1-203 Case Law Library
governance: Controlled citations. The classifier may cite ONLY entries in this file. No LLM-invented citations. Each entry states its holding narrowly. Verify URLs against primary sources before external distribution.

cross_cutting.citation: UCC §1-203 — Lease Distinguished from Security Interest
cross_cutting.holding: Two-part test: per se bright-line under subsection (b); residual economic-realities analysis under subsection (a).

cross_cutting.citation: Frank Lyon Co. v. United States, 435 U.S. 561 (1978)
cross_cutting.holding: Supreme Court substance-over-form doctrine; cited for tax and UCC characterization when parties structure a lease to obscure a secured financing.

cases.citation: In re Pillowtex, Inc. (Duke Energy Royal, LLC v. Pillowtex Corp.), 349 F.3d 711 (3d Cir. 2003)
cases.holding: Leading circuit authority on the economic-realities test. Even where none of the four per se factors are met, a transaction is a secured financing where the aggregate present value of rents exceeds equipment cost. Framework: (a) is the purchase option nominal; (b) do payments have PV >= equipment cost; (c) does the lease term cover total useful life.

cases.citation: In re QDS Components, Inc., 292 B.R. 313 (Bankr. S.D. Ohio 2002)
cases.holding: Ohio-law leading opinion on §1-203 recharacterization. A lease with a 'capital lease provision' — automatic ownership transfer, bargain purchase, or economic equivalent — is a per se security agreement under §1-203(b). Extended analysis of 'nominal consideration.'

cases.citation: Sunshine Heifers, LLC v. Citizens First Bank (In re Purdy), 763 F.3d 513 (6th Cir. 2014)
cases.holding: Where the lessor retains a meaningful reversionary interest — including a residual value guaranty rather than a bargain purchase — the transaction is a true lease. Ultimate test: did the lessor keep a 'meaningful reversionary interest' in the goods.

cases.citation: Leasing Service Corp. v. First Tennessee Bank, 826 F.2d 434 (6th Cir. 1987)
cases.holding: Older Sixth Circuit authority applying pre-revision UCC §1-201(37); retains relevance for the meaningful-residual and lessee equity-buildup factors.

cases.citation: In re Grubbs Construction Co., 319 B.R. 698 (Bankr. M.D. Fla. 2005)
cases.holding: Master Lease over five equipment schedules held not true leases but Article 9 security agreements because the lessee was effectively compelled to become owner at end of term.

cases.citation: In re Pierce Industries / Fifth Circuit line of cases (Chapman & Cutler commentary)
cases.holding: Fifth Circuit consistently applies §1-203's two-part test and looks past the parties' labels to economic substance.

cases.citation: In re WorldCom, Inc., 339 B.R. 56 (Bankr. S.D.N.Y. 2006)
cases.holding: Leading NY-law application. Failure to satisfy the bright-line test under §1-203(b) merely triggers §1-203(a) case-by-case analysis of whether the lessor retained a meaningful reversionary interest.

cases.citation: Pactel Fin. v. D.C. Marine Serv. Corp., 136 Misc.2d 194, 518 N.Y.S.2d 317 (N.Y. Dist. Ct. 1987)
cases.holding: Three-factor economic-realities inquiry: (a) nominal purchase option, (b) PV of rents >= original cost, (c) lease term covers total useful life.

cases.citation: In re Southeastern Materials, Inc., Bankr. M.D.N.C. 2010
cases.holding: Applying N.C. Gen. Stat. §25-1-203: where the lease is non-terminable by the lessee and includes a $1.00 end-of-term purchase option, the bright-line test is satisfied and the agreement creates a security interest as a matter of law. Directly on point for $1 buyout transactions.

cases.citation: In re Financial Computer Systems, Inc., 474 F.2d 1258 (9th Cir. 1973)
cases.holding: Under pre-revision §1-201(37): a lease-with-option-to-become-owner for nominal consideration is a lease intended for security. Ninth Circuit BAP decisions applying current §1-203 continue the per se-first, economic-realities-second framework.

cases.citation: In re Estate of Reifschneider and Kansas Bankruptcy Court car-lease line (Weil Restructuring Roundup commentary)
cases.holding: Kansas applies the two-prong test: (1) non-terminable by lessee, and (2) satisfaction of any one of the four §1-203(b) conditions.

OH.note: Ohio is the governing law of EFG's standard-form lease (§24). Cite in this order.

ordered_citations.citation: In re QDS Components, Inc., 292 B.R. 313 (Bankr. S.D. Ohio 2002)

ordered_citations.holding: Bright-line and economic-realities tests as adopted in Ohio.

ordered_citations.citation: Ohio Rev. Code Chapter 1309 (Ohio's UCC Article 9)
ordered_citations.holding: Statutory framework governing perfection, priority, and remedies.

ordered_citations.citation: Leasing Service Corp. v. First Tennessee Bank, 826 F.2d 434 (6th Cir. 1987)
ordered_citations.holding: Persuasive Sixth Circuit authority on meaningful residual and lessee equity-buildup.

nominal_consideration.treatment: Universally nominal (In re Southeastern Materials; In re QDS Components).
Not nominal only when tied to fair-market-value expectation (Chapman Bankruptcy Desk Reference).

nominal_consideration.value: >= 25% of FMV at end of term

nominal_consideration.treatment: Expressly not a security interest per §1-203(c)(6).
